01

Setting specification

Task

Find an approximate second-order stationary point of the population objective $f(x)=\mathbb{E}_Z[\ell(x;Z)]$. The gradient and Hessian tests both use this expectation objective.

Find an approximate second-order stationary point of the full objective:

$$\|\nabla f(\widehat{x})\|_2\le\varepsilon_g,\qquad\nabla^2f(\widehat{x})\succeq-\varepsilon_H I_d.$$

Admissible model

The population objective $f(x)=\mathbb{E}_Z[\ell(x;Z)]$ is bounded below.

The objective has a finite infimum, and the public initial point $x_0$ satisfies $f(x_0)-\inf_{x\in \mathbb{R}^d}f(x)\le\Delta$.

On a common probability-one event, all sample gradients are $\beta$-Lipschitz and all sample Hessians are $M_2$-Lipschitz at every point. Differentiation and expectation may be interchanged.

Sample errors satisfy $\|\nabla\ell(x;Z)-\nabla f(x)\|_2\le\sigma_1$ and $\|\nabla^2\ell(x;Z)-\nabla^2f(x)\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le\sigma_2$, with $\sup_x\|\nabla f(x)\|_2\le G$.

Oracle interface

An opaque persistent handle $a$ can be requested for free without revealing sample data. Distinct new handles bind independent samples $Z_a$. At each call, choose an existing handle and any point $(a,x)$, then request the full $\nabla\ell(x;Z_a)$ or full $\nabla^2\ell(x;Z_a)$, charged separately. A handle may be reused at arbitrarily many points.

No sample value, internal sample data or third derivative is returned. An observed full matrix may be used freely in internal linear algebra.

The public inputs are $x_0$, the target accuracy, and $d$, $\Delta$, $\beta$, $M_2$, $\sigma_1$, $\sigma_2$, $G$, $\varepsilon_g$, $\varepsilon_H$. Numerical constants are admissible bounds and need not equal the sharp constants of the instance. The objective, unqueried derivatives, minimizer and minimum value are hidden.

Output

Return $\widehat{x}\in \mathbb{R}^d$.

The output may be an unqueried point, a feasible average of past iterates, or another feasible postprocessing result. No function value or additional computable certificate is required.

The algorithm may output the failure symbol $\bot$; this event counts toward the failure probability.

Loss or accuracy criterion

Scale the gradient norm and the negative-curvature residual by their respective tolerances. The base error is the larger scaled residual, so a value at most one means that both tolerances are met.

The base error is

$$\mathcal{E}(\widehat{x})=\max\left\{\frac{\|\nabla f(\widehat{x})\|_2}{\varepsilon_g},\frac{[-\lambda_{\min}(\nabla^2f(\widehat{x}))]_+}{\varepsilon_H}\right\}.$$

$[a]_+=\max\{a,0\}$, and $\lambda_{\min}$ denotes the smallest eigenvalue of a symmetric matrix. The target is $\mathcal{E}(\widehat{x})\le1$, where $\varepsilon_g$ and $\varepsilon_H$ are independent positive tolerances.

Resource accounting

The native cost is the joint resource vector $(N_g,N_H)$, counting full sample gradients and full sample Hessians separately. Requesting both derivatives at one point costs two calls, as does evaluating the same handle at two points for a difference.

The total-cost projection is explicitly $N_g+N_H$. Separate budgets for $N_g$ and $N_H$ may also be displayed, but displaying one coordinate does not make the other operation free. All coordinatewise upper bounds must be attained by the same algorithm.

The resource budget is a fixed worst-case cap on every execution path. Initialization, stopping checks, and all actual responses in a batch are included.

Arithmetic, linear algebra, tensor operations, storage, and global solution of known models are free. Bit complexity, communication, and wall-clock time are not counted.

Algorithm views and success guarantees

Arbitrary measurable adaptive algorithms with private randomness are allowed.

No linear-span, Krylov or zero-respecting restriction is imposed. Memory and internal computation are unrestricted.

Information is acquired adaptively in query order. Parallel submission does not reduce the number of actual responses counted. There is no communication-round or memory budget. Exact real arithmetic and arbitrarily small positive query separations are allowed.

Choose one algorithm from the public inputs, then require its guarantee separately for every admissible instance and oracle law.

$$\Pr\!\left[\max\left\{\frac{\|\nabla f(\widehat{x})\|_2}{\varepsilon_g},\frac{[-\lambda_{\min}(\nabla^2f(\widehat{x}))]_+}{\varepsilon_H}\right\}\le 1\right]\ge\frac23.$$

Expectation or probability is evaluated after fixing the instance; randomness comes from the algorithm's private seed and oracle sampling.

The running-cost guarantee is specified separately under RESOURCE.

02

Notation and parameters

$x,\widehat{x},x_0$

Query or decision point, algorithm output, and public initial point.

Domain
$\mathbb{R}^d$
$\mathbb{R}^d$

Real coordinate space; vectors use the Euclidean norm unless otherwise stated.

Domain
$d$ is a positive integer.
$\langle u,v\rangle,\ \|u\|_2$

Euclidean inner product and norm.

$$\langle u,v\rangle=u^\top v,\qquad\|u\|_2=\sqrt{\langle u,u\rangle}.$$

$D^jf(x),\ \nabla f(x),\ \nabla^2f(x)$

Fréchet derivative of order $j$, gradient and Hessian.

Domain
$j\in\{0,\ldots,2\}$ and $D^0f=f$.
$\|T\|_{\mathrm{op}},\ \|T\|_{\mathrm{op},2}$

Induced operator norm of a Euclidean multilinear tensor; the spectral norm for matrices.

$$\|T\|_{\mathrm{op}}=\|T\|_{\mathrm{op},2}=\sup_{\|u_1\|_2,\ldots,\|u_j\|_2\le1}|T[u_1,\ldots,u_j]|.$$

$\mathcal{E}$

Base error defined in the metric specification; expectation or probability aggregation is imposed by the guarantee.

$N$

Total number of original oracle calls; the unit cost is specified in the resource convention.

Domain
$N\in\mathbb{Z}_{\ge0}$.
$T^*$

Minimum worst-case budget for one algorithm to meet the requirement on the full instance class, within the specified regime, guarantee and resource projection. Expected-resource specifications instead minimize the per-instance expected budget.

$O,\Omega,\Theta,\widetilde{O}$

Asymptotic upper bounds, lower bounds, matching bounds up to constants, and upper bounds omitting the declared logarithmic factors.

Domain
Hidden constants, fixed parameters, and omitted logarithmic variables are specified for each bound.
$\inf,\sup,\min,\max$

Infimum, supremum, attained minimum and attained maximum.

$c,C$

Positive universal constants without assigned numerical values; a subscript permits dependence only on the indicated fixed parameters.

Domain
$0<c,C<\infty$.
$f,f^*$

Unknown objective and its global infimum over the specified feasible domain.

$$f^*=\inf_{x\in \mathbb{R}^d}f(x).$$

$\mathbb{E},\Pr$

Expectation and probability after fixing the instance; their randomness sources are specified by the guarantee.

$Z,\ell(x;Z)$

Sample random variable and the associated scalar sample loss.

$$f(x)=\mathbb{E}_Z\ell(x;Z).$$

$a,Z_a$

Opaque persistent handle and its associated hidden sample.

$N_g,N_H$

Numbers of full sample-gradient and full sample-Hessian evaluations.

Domain
$N_g,N_H\in\mathbb{Z}_{\ge0}$.
$\bot$

Output symbol explicitly declaring algorithmic failure.

$u\preceq v$

Coordinatewise order for resource vectors; the same symbol for symmetric matrices denotes the positive semidefinite order.

$$u\preceq v\iff u_i\le v_i\quad\text{for every }i.$$

$\lambda_{\min}(A),[z]_+$

The smallest eigenvalue of a symmetric matrix and the positive part of a scalar.

$$[z]_+=\max\{z,0\}.$$

$I_d$

The identity matrix in dimension $d$.

$d$

Ambient dimension; dimension requirements are stated separately for each bound.

Domain
$d\in\mathbb{N}_{\ge 1}$
$\Delta$

Upper bound on the difference between the objective value at the known initial point and its global infimum.

Domain
$\Delta>0$
$\beta$

Common Lipschitz upper bound for the gradients of all sample losses.

Domain
$\beta>0$
$M_2$

Common Lipschitz upper bound for the Hessians of all sample losses.

Domain
$M_2>0$
$\sigma_1$

Almost-sure bound on the sample gradient's deviation from the population gradient.

Domain
$\sigma_1>0$
$\sigma_2$

Almost-sure operator-norm bound on the sample Hessian's deviation from the population Hessian.

Domain
$\sigma_2>0$
$G$

Global upper bound on the population gradient norm

Domain
$G>0$
$\varepsilon_g$

Gradient tolerance

Domain
$\varepsilon_g>0$
$\varepsilon_H$

Curvature tolerance

Domain
$\varepsilon_H>0$
$\theta$

Fixed group of positive model bounds.

$$\theta=(\Delta,\beta,M_2,\sigma_1,\sigma_2,G).$$

$B_g$

Dimensionless leading term in one algorithm's gradient-evaluation budget.

$$B_g=1+\frac{\Delta\beta+\sigma_1^2}{\varepsilon_g^2}+\frac{\sigma_1\beta\Delta}{\varepsilon_g^3}+\frac{\beta^2\Delta}{\varepsilon_g^2\varepsilon_H}.$$

$B_H$

Dimensionless leading term in one algorithm's Hessian-evaluation budget.

$$B_H=1+\frac{\Delta\beta}{\varepsilon_g^2}+\frac{\sigma_2^2}{\varepsilon_H^2}+\frac{\sigma_2M_2\Delta}{\varepsilon_g\varepsilon_H^2}+\frac{2M_2^2\Delta}{\varepsilon_H^3}.$$

$T,\Lambda$

Iteration cap and shared logarithmic factor.

$$T=\left\lceil1+48\Delta\left(\frac{32\beta}{3\varepsilon_g^2}+\frac{12M_2^2}{\varepsilon_H^3}\right)\right\rceil,\quad\Lambda=1+\log[C(d+1)(T+1)].$$

$s_*$

Positive scale used in the lower-bound construction.

$$s_*=\min\{1,\sigma_1,\sigma_2,\beta,M_2,G\}.$$

$D_g$

Logarithmic dimension factor in the persistent-handle gradient hard construction.

$$D_g=C\log(2+\Delta/\varepsilon_g+\Delta s_*^2/\varepsilon_g^3).$$

$d_*$

Sufficient dimension threshold for the lower-bound construction; an existential constant function, not a supplied numerical value.

$$d_*\le C(\theta)\left[1+\frac{\Delta D_g^{3/4}}{\varepsilon_g}+\varepsilon_H^{-4}\log(2/\varepsilon_H)+\varepsilon_H^{-3}\right].$$

/proofs/0/proof_steps/0 · SHA-256 6d3cbff27ca362928edf56273844ce8472bae3a8e6b8e56b784af47298d6ee37
Translate the public initial point to the origin. Set e=epsilon_g, b=sigma_1/2 and t=x_1-(x_0)_1. For hypotheses h=+2e and h=-2e, let independent handle variables Z take values +/-b with mean h. Define ell_h(x;Z)=4e*sqrt(1+t^2)+Z*t, independent of all other coordinates. Its population objective is 4e*sqrt(1+t^2)+h*t.
Native item 2
/proofs/0/proof_steps/1 · SHA-256 575ac83107ad71ed2c1132086cfbf09a2c6daf7a8b993816824b20a0909fd8c1
These populations have finite minima 2*sqrt(3)*e and initial gap (4-2*sqrt(3))*e. Their gradient norm is at most 6e. Each sample Hessian has only entry 4e*(1+t^2)^(-3/2), so sample-gradient Lipschitz constant is at most 4e and sample-Hessian Lipschitz constant is at most 12e. Gradient noise is at most b+2e<=sigma_1; Hessian noise is zero. Differentiation commutes with expectation. The r7 inequalities therefore ensure every fixed-contract assumption. Only the population must be bounded below; individual sample losses need not be.
Native item 3
/proofs/0/proof_steps/2 · SHA-256 2f1a1238c84c5c744144e44afc11eff165dd4111741b0c8285d9f23656681702
The population Hessian is positive semidefinite, so any positive epsilon_H is allowed. Under h=+2e, any successful output must have t<0; under h=-2e it must have t>0. Failure symbols count as failure. Thus success probability >=2/3 separately on both admissible instances yields a test with total variation at least 1/3.
Native item 4
/proofs/0/proof_steps/3 · SHA-256 7c7f6249b118f08550a2dec5a6976bbdb87e4aa99b265cd41cc9101a580a7008
All Hessian responses are deterministic and identical under both hypotheses, even at arbitrary adaptive points. The first gradient query on a handle reveals its single Z; later gradient queries on that handle add no information. Handles first used for Hessians still reveal no Z until their first gradient. Opaque handle allocation supplies no side data. Padding by unused coordinates preserves these facts for every d>=1 and arbitrary outputs.
Native item 5
/proofs/0/proof_steps/4 · SHA-256 a381b5176a311bbf6679d497b00fdba81e552592b8aa7eaef379eec9cac541ad
Let a=2e/b<=1/2. The two Bernoulli laws have probabilities (1+a)/2 and (1-a)/2. Their KL divergence is a*log((1+a)/(1-a))<=4a^2=16e^2/b^2. Adaptive transcript chain-rule accounting bounds KL by (16e^2/b^2)*n when the worst-case gradient cap is n, regardless of the finite Hessian cap. Reuse contributes zero new conditional divergence.
Native item 6
/proofs/0/proof_steps/5 · SHA-256 3f09206796656622408b8cefe25ebccdca4f8182938f350a292c27d97525f198
Pinsker's inequality as used in Appendix C gives KL>=2*(1/3)^2=2/9. Consequently n>=b^2/(72e^2)=sigma_1^2/(288e^2). This holds for every feasible algorithm, hence also for the q2 minimax infimum. The threshold and coefficient are explicit and uniform in all nine native parameters. The extension from the source's one-dimensional construction to arbitrary finite d is the flat-coordinate embedding above; no target subclass assumption is added.

/proofs/1/body · SHA-256 35ef02782753222040f20776badc7d6824b5958da8ae628a7bcf24a599584955
The frozen b6/p1 establishes Ng>=L=sigma1^2/(288epsilon_g^2) on exact r7 for every successful algorithm, with arbitrary finite Hessian budget. For each same algorithm and each path,Ng+NH>=Ng becauseNH>=0. Thus any successful total-budget algorithm must have totalcap>=L. Likewise a successful jointcap(Bg,BH) must satisfy Bg>=L. Equivalently B subset{(Bg,BH)>=0:Bg>=L}. Infima over identical algorithm/instance/guarantee classes preserve these implications. This is not equality or identity of q1/q2/q4: new quantity-matched bounds carry explicit directions. No reverse implication, Hessianlower, sum-to-gradientlower or mixing of different algorithm minima is claimed. The oldr7 guard remains exact; onr3 intersectr7 maximize the old total lower and this newL, even if one is dominated. The proof also records that a single algorithm with jointcap(C,0) gives the three marginal upper witnesses, but not a pair formed from different optimizers. The retained older q1 lower Lold on exact r3 also implies, for the same algorithm class, the joint necessary sum halfspace Bg+BH>=Lold on r3. This implication is separately published as b14; it yields no positive Ng or NH marginal lower alone and is not asserted outside r3.

/proofs/2/body · SHA-256 dcbcd608b71c27f405399666b14d8c2af14585cb5728bf9619348ac03943332c
# HOS06: An explicit witness with finitely many gradient calls and zero Hessian calls (pending independent review) This round is an analyst_derivation guided by user feedback, not an outcome of the earlier blind scout, and confers no additional credit for earlier native source_read or approvals. The argument establishes only the single-coordinate q3 claim and a joint-budget witness for the same algorithm; it does not combine the minimum gradient cost of another algorithm with zero Hessian cost. Contract basis: in the new previous-baseline, on a single common probability-1 event, the sample losses have globally β-Lipschitz gradients and M2-Lipschitz Hessians; the population objective has initial gap≤Δ; distinct new handles are independent, and the same handle may be reused across points; the gradient error is ≤σ1 almost surely; all public structural parameters β,M2,Δ,σ1,σ2,G are strictly positive, with d≥1 and 0<εg,εH≤1. Thus this proof does not tacitly exclude β=0/M2=0: these cases were already outside the native structural domain. Queries range over the entire space. Population differentiation and expectation may be interchanged; the native resources Ng,NH are counted separately, the failure symbol ⊥ is permitted, and per-instance success≥2/3 together with a finite resource cap on every execution path is required. ## Public parameters and fixed caps Let \[ a=\min\{\varepsilon_g/8,\varepsilon_H^2/(48M_2)\},\quad b=\varepsilon_H/4,\quad D=\min\{\varepsilon_g^2/(16\beta),\varepsilon_H^3/(16M_2^2)\}, \] \[ K=\lfloor\Delta/D\rfloor+1,\quad m_g=\max\{1,\lceil6K\sigma_1^2/a^2\rceil\},\quad m_H=\max\{1,\lceil24Kd\beta^2/b^2\rceil\},\quad h=b/(M_2\sqrt d). \] These quantities depend only on the public inputs and are all positive and finite. Let \[ C_{\rm gf}=K(m_g+2dm_H). \] No attempt is made to optimize this highly conservative gradient cap; its purpose is to establish a single finite witness valid throughout the contract, rather than to claim optimal gradient complexity. ## Estimators: gradient oracle calls only At the current point x: 1. Request one sample gradient from each of mg previously unused new handles and take their average \(\widetilde g\). Conditional on the past, independence, unbiasedness, and an error second moment ≤σ1² give \[ \Pr(\|\widetilde g-\nabla f(x)\|>a\mid\text{past})\le\sigma_1^2/(m_ga^2)\le1/(6K). \] 2. When a curvature check is needed, draw another mH independent new handles; for each handle a, request two gradients \(\nabla\ell(x\pm he_j;Z_a)\) along each coordinate axis at the same x. Use the central differences as matrix columns to obtain D_a, symmetrize to \(A_a=(D_a+D_a^T)/2\), and take \(\widetilde H=m_H^{-1}\sum A_a\). Neither a sample Hessian nor a sample value is requested. Each column of D_a has norm ≤β, so \(\|A_a\|_F\le\sqrt d\beta\). The M2-Lipschitz property of the sample Hessian gives a central-difference error ≤M2 h/2 in each column; therefore \[ \|\mathbb E A_a-\nabla^2f(x)\|_{op}\le\sqrt d M_2h/2=b/2. \] Symmetrization does not increase the error in the Frobenius/operator norms. The Hilbert-space variance of the independent sample matrices satisfies \[ \mathbb E\|\widetilde H-\mathbb EA_a\|_F^2\le d\beta^2/m_H. \] Thus Chebyshev and op≤F give \[ \Pr(\|\widetilde H-\nabla^2 f(x)\|_{op}>b\mid\text{current gradient and past}) \le4d\beta^2/(m_Hb^2)\le1/(6K). \] Reuse occurs only among the 2d finite-difference gradients for a single new handle. Handles within the matrix batch are independent; the gradient batch and the matrix batch are independent; and new batches are independent across iterations. The conditional bounds hold uniformly for adaptively selected x, without incorrectly treating reused noise as independent. The common probability-1 sample-smoothness event makes all adaptive locations simultaneously valid. ## Truncated algorithm Starting from the public x0, execute at most K iterations: - Form \(\widetilde g\). If \(\|\widetilde g\|>\varepsilon_g/2\), set \(x\gets x-\widetilde g/\beta\) and proceed to the next iteration. - Otherwise, form \(\widetilde H\). If \(\lambda_{min}(\widetilde H)\ge-3\varepsilon_H/4\), return the current x. - Otherwise, take a unit eigenvector v corresponding to the smallest eigenvalue of the known symmetric matrix, choose its sign so that \(\widetilde g^Tv\le0\), and set \(x\gets x+(\varepsilon_H/M_2)v\). If K iterations are reached without returning, output ⊥. Eigendecomposition of a known matrix, inner products, and linear algebra are all free internal operations; sign selection and termination verification require no additional information/function-value calls. Use a fixed measurable eigenvector-selection rule; tied eigenvalues do not affect the inequalities. h and every step are finite, positive/known; all loops are truncated, so the per-path cap is retained even when the estimates are inaccurate. ## Joint good event, descent, and accuracy There are at most K gradient estimates and K matrix estimates. A union bound using the conditional failure bounds gives a good-event probability ≥1−2K/(6K)=2/3. All conditions below hold on this same event. If a gradient step is taken, a≤εg/8 and \(\|\widetilde g\|>\varepsilon_g/2\). β-smoothness gives \[ f(x-\widetilde g/\beta)-f(x) \le-\|\widetilde g\|^2/(2\beta)+a\|\widetilde g\|/\beta \le-\varepsilon_g^2/(16\beta). \] If a negative-curvature step is taken, \(v^T\nabla^2 f(x)v<-\varepsilon_H/2\), while \(\nabla f(x)^Tv\le a\). The population Hessian is also M2-Lipschitz. Set s=εH/M2; the Taylor upper bound then gives \[ f(x+sv)-f(x)\le as-\varepsilon_Hs^2/4+M_2s^3/6 \le-\varepsilon_H^3/(16M_2^2). \] Hence every nonterminating step decreases the objective by at least D. Since K D>Δ, all K steps cannot be nonterminating on the good event, as that would violate f(x0)−inf f≤Δ. At termination (including a threshold attained with equality), \[ \|\nabla f(x)\|\le\varepsilon_g/2+a\le5\varepsilon_g/8\le\varepsilon_g, \qquad \lambda_{min}(\nabla^2f(x))\ge-3\varepsilon_H/4-b=-\varepsilon_H. \] The algorithm therefore satisfies both SOS conditions at the same point with probability at least 2/3, and on every execution path \[ N_g\le C_{\rm gf}<\infty,\qquad N_H=0. \] The nonnegativity of q3 gives the matching lower bound 0, so the Hessian single-coordinate optimum is exactly 0. This conclusion does not state Ng=0 or total=0; the jointly attainable budget of this same witness is \((C_{\rm gf},0)\) and its upward closure. It cannot be combined with the q2 optimum of a different algorithm to obtain a smaller joint budget. ## Online literature verification actually performed in this round and limits of adoption The [original SPIDER paper arXiv:1807.01695v2](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1807.01695v2) was actually opened and read: §3.1 Assumptions1–3 (PDF pp9–10), §3.3 Algorithm2/Theorem6 (pp14–15), footnote 9 on success-probability amplification, and the beginning of Appendix B.4. The paper does construct an SOS algorithm using stochastic gradients; its sample conditions are compatible with this native contract. Direct adoption, however, would also require addressing internal accuracy, verification/restarts from 1/2 to 2/3, and per-path accounting. Accordingly, this candidate does not claim to have completed a transfer of the full SPIDER proof and does not adopt its optimized gradient rate; the zero-Hessian conclusion is supported by the independent explicit finite algorithm above. This report does not reprove the full appendix or the Neon2 proof.

The complete new finite capped proof HOS06_GRADIENT_ONLY_SOSP_20261116 explicitly certifies a SAME algorithm with Ng<=Cgf<infinity and NH=0 on every execution path, and simultaneous population SOS success>=2/3 on the entire same r2 target. Zero is no larger than the old nonnegative sufficient upper cap, so that historical upper may remain a valid conditional statement while being dominated in c3's selected envelope. It is supported by the new exact-zero witness and nonnegativity, never by a claim that the full published b2 object was unchanged. c3 uses new b9/b10 to certify exact0. No zero Ng, zero total, independently optimized joint pair, or source-guard extension follows. Outside the unchanged target no result is added.

/joint_analysis/impact/3/argument · SHA-256 e4f77f38555537082448312bca8e2618d950ced10eb13e11ebc95c0575dc2423
Publish separately proved directed resource projections: Ng>=Lg implies Ntotal>=Lg and Bg>=Lg, preserving r7; the old total lower also gives Bg+BH>=Lold only on its own r3. A complete same-algorithm finite gradient-estimation/central-difference/negative-curvature witness has NH=0 and public finite worst-path Ng, success at least 2/3. It closes only the Hessian coordinate and supplies its own joint vector; do not combine optimal coordinates from different algorithms. This revision addresses the preserved actual independent-review issues. Publication and typed projection obligations are explicit; every mathematical formula and adoption guard is verified against the exact native candidate, and historical effects are not reported as new frontier gains. Operational read priority after the preserved incomplete 40-tool review: finish the full prepared joint_analysis first, read exact decisive baseline parent objects completely where useful, and finish all evidence/resource/proof objects required by the review pack. Forty-eight tool calls allow completion of the same strict source, exact-reference, prepared-hash and six-check gates; no prior reading or approval is imported.

/joint_analysis/target/full_domain · SHA-256 18cffcbcf2e22897c060a80d6c3f9f73795ea9a55cf85cea7ff1cbe6836abe22
r4 (the fixed reusable-handle contract): integer d>=1, positive Delta,beta,M_2,sigma_1,sigma_2,G, and independent 0<epsilon_g,epsilon_H<=1. Primary fixed-scale asymptotics vary d and both tolerances jointly. Native q1/q4 fix the six structural bounds; q2/q3 retain all nine tracked parameters and their explicit uniform formulas (their comparison constant_dependencies are empty). No quantity metadata is changed. The guarantee is main/g1, per-instance success >=2/3, with worst-case native vector (N_g,N_H), and exactly the declared q1 sum, q2 gradient, q3 Hessian and q4 vector projections.
